title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair loop changes verifier-detected safety violations of LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 deterministic intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal (requested model: gpt-5-mini) produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal examined by a deterministic netops validator with up to one automated repair iteration invoked only if the validator flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on that shared candidate. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002. The archived analysis used the exact McNemar two-sided convention implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); this yields two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed single discordant pair (implementation detail and bootstrap CI in Methods). Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; the marginal numeric verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though one archived discordant episode shows the loop corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being integrated into NetOps/AIOps workflows to translate operator intent into device configuration, to plan multi-step changes, and to propose repairs. Systems and surveys emphasize that production safety relies heavily on surrounding engineering—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback—rather than on the model alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A common operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): the model produces a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and automated or human-in-the-loop repairs are applied if violations are found. Despite broad adoption of this pattern, controlled measurements isolating the verifier’s marginal contribution while holding the model’s initial proposal fixed are rare. This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that answers a narrowly scoped operational question: given identical initial proposals, how much does integrating a deterministic verifier plus one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM alone?
sections.related_work: Formal network-configuration verification and header-space analyses provide deterministic checks for reachability, isolation, and update-safety and underpin many verifier implementations [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps work proposes LLM-based intent translators and highlights the need for validators and guardrails to achieve operational reliability (e.g., INTA, Confucius) [Wei et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate→verify→repair patterns appear across structured-generation domains and have been recommended as a practical method to reduce incorrect model outputs [Qu et al., 2026; Wang et al., 2025]. Failure-mode analyses document hallucination, overconfidence, and tool-integration errors that motivate verifier-in-the-loop designs [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. However, supplied system papers and surveys seldom provide controlled ablation measurements isolating verifier effect size under reproducible conditions. Our experiment contributes one such preregistered measurement and situates it relative to those system reports.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental plan: We preregistered the study (study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026). The confirmatory hypothesis tested whether an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration reduces verifier-detected high/medium-severity violations relative to the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration froze inclusion/exclusion rules, task-generator seeds, the analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule prior to any result inspection.

Task generation and stratification: We used a deterministic synthetic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) with preregistered seeds to produce 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified into VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167) and static-route-change (166) clusters. Task payloads constrain allowed_fields to {admin, mtu, vlan} to match the chosen verifier’s modeled features; tasks referencing unmodeled features would be routed to an 'unmodeled-feature' cohort and excluded from the primary analysis (no confirmatory exclusions occurred). Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, and an explicit required_sequence; representative task manifests are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl.

Generation semantics and experimental control: To isolate the marginal verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals we used preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" with independent_condition_generation = false. For each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal (the shared candidate) which served as the baseline output; the guarded condition validated that same shared candidate and invoked at most one automated repair iteration only if the validator flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. This design intentionally avoids verifier-guided regeneration and measures the incremental benefit of verification and a bounded repair budget for fixed proposals.

Models, adapter, and verifier: Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini called through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses); model configuration archived in execution/model_configuration.json (max_output_tokens = 2000, single-attempt generation semantics). The deterministic validator used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; the validator’s specification and the mapping from violation codes to severity levels are archived in the evidence bundle.

Statistical test and implementation details: The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. Our archived analysis executor implements the exact two-sided McNemar by (a) letting n = n10 + n01 be the number of discordant pairs and (b) testing the observed n10 under X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5). The two-sided p-value is computed as p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)}, truncated at 1.0. For small n this exact-binomial convention is conventional and is the implementation recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. We also compute paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals for the absolute difference using B = 10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729, resampling pairs with replacement while preserving pairing. All analysis parameters and code references are archived.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcome counts: The run completed per the preregistration with complete_pair_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 1000, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls = 1). Per-condition aggregated counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) is: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact McNemar two-sided p-value and CI: With discordant-pair total n = 1 and observed n10 = 1 the archived exact-binomial two-sided rule yields p_two-sided = 2 × min{0.5, 0.5} = 1.00. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729); bootstrap details and resampling code are archived under analysis/.

Repair activity and discordant-pair provenance: Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1 across all tasks. The archived execution and analysis artifacts attribute the single discordant outcome (n10 = 1) to that sole repair-stage invocation: the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass. The evidence bundle contains the per-task validator diagnostics and the repair-stage provider-call trace for that episode; the experiment manifest documents how to locate it deterministically (filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pairs where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation and guarded scoring indicates pass). Because only one such discordant pair exists, that filter returns the single episode and its repair prompt/response and validator violation-code trace for qualitative inspection. The validator-spec artifact in the bundle provides the mapping of violation codes to severity levels. Representative per-task exemplars and provider-call traces (including shared-initial candidate text) are included in execution/responses and execution/scoring subpaths.

Secondary analyses and power considerations: Planned secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative because observed violation counts were effectively zero; there were no meaningful class-level counts to support inference. The preregistration assumed a baseline violation prevalence near 0.30 for power planning; the observed baseline prevalence (1 failure in 500) was far lower, producing a ceiling effect that reduces statistical sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric. This mismatch between assumed and observed baseline rates explains the small absolute effect and the null exact p-value despite an observed correction in one episode.
sections.discussion:
Conditional interpretation: The experiment provides a conditional, artifact-backed estimate of verifier+single-repair impact under a narrow regime: single requested model family (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier limited to a small feature set (admin/mtu/vlan), and a repair budget of at most one automated iteration. Under these constraints the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals (baseline 499/500), so the measurable absolute pass-rate gain from the verifier on this metric was small (0.002). Importantly, the verifier did perform a concrete correction: the single repair-stage call converted one baseline failure into a pass. This demonstrates corrective potential even under low baseline error prevalence.

Design-choice implications: The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally measure the marginal benefit of verifier+repair for fixed proposals. Different operational semantics (e.g., verifier-guided regeneration, iterative repair, larger repair budgets) answer different operational tradeoffs and likely yield different effect sizes. Practitioners should select experimental semantics that mirror the intended deployment before estimating guardrail benefits.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic generator seeds, and automated exclusion rules; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity depends on whether the verifier’s modeled property set matches operator-critical safety constraints; our composite pass/fail is bounded by the verifier’s coverage and severity mapping (archived). External validity is limited: single model/validator pair and synthetic tasks constrained to a small command subset limit cross-vendor and production generalization. Conclusion validity: the extreme ceiling effect (very low baseline failure rate) undermines power for detecting small absolute improvements; the preregistered power calculation assumed a much higher baseline error rate.

Operational recommendations supported by the archive: (1) Measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative operational data before investing in expensive repair budgets—when baseline error is already very low, marginal pass-rate gains from verifier+repair may be small for the pass-rate metric. (2) Design verifiers whose modeled properties align with operator-critical safety constraints; inspect validator-spec artifacts to evaluate coverage. (3) Choose generation semantics (shared-initial vs verifier-guided regeneration) that match deployment priorities: shared-initial minimizes regeneration, verifier-guided maximizes final-pass probability at the cost of additional model calls. The archived logs and exemplar repair traces support operation-level cost/benefit analyses.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On the supplied synthetic verifier-scoped corpus and with the requested model/validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the two-sided exact-binomial convention). The outcome documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal error prevalence is extremely low and verifier coverage is constrained, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit on this metric may be negligible, though verifiers can still correct rare concrete failures (one archived corrected episode). We recommend operators measure baseline error prevalence, verify verifier coverage for their safety-critical properties, and align generation/repair semantics with operational priorities. All artifacts required for deterministic re-inspection are archived in the evidence bundle referenced below and in the Disclosure Statement.

Generation semantics and model-call accounting (artifact-backed): preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' with independent_condition_generation = false: for each task the pipeline produced a single shared initial LLM proposal that served as the baseline and was also validated by the guarded arm; the guarded arm invoked a repair-stage provider call only when the validator reported preregistered high/medium-severity violations on that shared candidate. Repairs: the guarded arm permitted up to one automated repair iteration per preregistration; observed repairs = 1. Exclusions and missingness: zero confirmatory pairs were excluded. limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; the task payloads in the archive show allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not necessarily generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 must be interpreted in that context and reflects the archived two-sided exact-binomial convention for n = 1 discordant pair.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair_id entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
